decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY recording the approved higher-power PWM controllers and 50A adapter. The reserve-capacity rationale belongs to the electrical-load Requirement and does not require another BOM attribute.
Approval of the 50A AC/DC adapter and higher-power controllers does not replace or modify the requirement to use a standard 120V wall outlet.
The approved power components provide electrical capacity but do not change the established 0-to-3000 RPM adjustment range or intended speed modes.
The electrical-capacity decision does not change bowl capacity, depth, geometry, or enclosure-size constraints.
Preventing power-system overheating is distinct from preventing liquid leakage into electrical components; the isolation requirement remains unchanged.
The approved power supply and controllers do not modify the existing splash target or accepted mechanical mitigation methods.
Selecting particular higher-capacity components does not change the existing strategy of using simple off-the-shelf electronics for the first prototype.
The component approval supplies design inputs for the wiring plan but does not change the requirement to deliver a basic wiring plan or establish a new wiring-plan attribute.
Additional capacity for simultaneous solenoid operation supports implementation but does not change the dispensing mechanism, sequence, or required flow behavior.
Reserve electrical capacity intended to prevent overheating does not alter the existing motor durability or maximum-speed duty constraints.
The approved electrical components are inputs to later layout work, but the source does not establish a changed CAD geometry or invalidate the existing motor-accommodation requirement.
The electrical-capacity decision does not change the required mixing quality, foam outcome, whisk selection, positioning, or high-speed mixing behavior.
